solution: At \(m\) minutes past 2 the angle is \(5.5m - 60\) degrees. Setting \(5.5m - 60 = 90\) gives \(m = \frac{300}{11} = 27\frac{3}{11}\), so the hands are at right angles at about 2:27.
At 4:00 the minute hand is on 12 and the hour hand on 4, four hour-marks apart. Each mark is \(30^\circ\), so the angle is \(4 \times 30^\circ = 120^\circ\).
At 5:30 the hour hand is at \(5 \times 30^\circ + 30 \times 0.5^\circ = 165^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(180^\circ\). The angle between them is \(15^\circ\).
In a straight line (but not together) the hands are \(180^\circ\) apart. At \(m\) minutes past 3, \(5.5m - 90 = 180\) gives \(m = \frac{540}{11} = 49\frac{1}{11}\), so about 3:49.
At 9:20 the hour hand is at \(9 \times 30^\circ + 20 \times 0.5^\circ = 280^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(120^\circ\). The angle between them is \(160^\circ\).

At 10:40 the hour hand is at \(10 \times 30^\circ + 40 \times 0.5^\circ = 320^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(240^\circ\), so the smaller angle is \(80^\circ\). The reflex angle is \(360^\circ - 80^\circ = 280^\circ\).
In 12 hours the hands are at right angles twice in every hour except two (around 3 and 9 the two occasions are shared), which is 22 times. In a day that is \(2 \times 22 = 44\) times.
At \(m\) minutes past 1 the angle is \(5.5m - 30\) degrees. Setting it to 72 gives \(m = \frac{204}{11} = 18\frac{6}{11}\), so the angle is \(72^\circ\) at about 1:18.

At \(m\) minutes past 8 the hour hand is \(240 + 0.5m\) degrees round and the minute hand \(6m\). They are \(90^\circ\) apart when \(5.5m = 150\) or \(5.5m = 330\), that is \(m = 27\frac{3}{11}\) or \(m = 60\), so at about 8:27 and at 9:00.
At 2:38 the hour hand is at \(2 \times 30^\circ + 38 \times 0.5^\circ = 79^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(38 \times 6^\circ = 228^\circ\). The angle between them is \(149^\circ\).
At \(6^\circ\) per minute, 45 minutes take the minute hand through \(45 \times 6^\circ = 270^\circ\).
The hour hand turns \(30^\circ\) an hour, that is \(0.5^\circ\) a minute. In 20 minutes it moves \(20 \times 0.5^\circ = 10^\circ\).
There are 1440 minutes in a day, and the hands coincide every \(65\frac{5}{11}\) minutes. That gives \(\frac{1440}{720/11} = 22\) times.
At \(m\) minutes past 4 the angle is \(5.5m - 120\) degrees once the minute hand has passed the hour hand. Setting it to 90 gives \(m = \frac{420}{11} = 38\frac{2}{11}\), so about 4:38.
Gaining 5 minutes an hour, the clock is \(6 \times 5 = 30\) minutes ahead after 6 hours. At 6:00 PM it shows 6:30 PM.
Losing 4 minutes an hour, the clock is \(5 \times 4 = 20\) minutes behind after 5 hours. At 1:00 PM it shows 12:40 PM.
Twelve hours contain four 3-hour spells, each gaining 10 minutes, so the clock is 40 minutes ahead. At 9:00 PM it shows 9:40 PM.
Twelve hours contain six 2-hour spells, each losing 5 minutes, so the clock is 30 minutes behind. At 6:00 PM it shows 5:30 PM.
From 1:00 AM to 1:00 PM is 12 hours, and the clock gains \(12 \times 12 = 144\) minutes, that is 2 hours 24 minutes. It shows 3:24 PM.
From 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM is 9 hours, and the watch loses \(9 \times 3 = 27\) minutes. It shows 5:33 PM.
The clock is 20 minutes fast and loses 4 minutes an hour, so it is right after \(\frac{20}{4} = 5\) hours. That is at 11:00 AM.
The clock is 18 minutes fast and loses 6 minutes an hour, so it is right after \(\frac{18}{6} = 3\) hours. That is at 1:00 PM.
Losing 1 minute in every 5, the watch shows \(\frac{4}{5}\) of the real time passed. In 3 hours (180 minutes) it advances 144 minutes, so it shows 2:24 PM.
Twelve hours contain six 2-hour spells, each gaining 10 minutes, so the clock is an hour ahead. At 4:00 PM it shows 5:00 PM.
From 6:00 AM to 12:00 PM is 6 hours, and the clock gains \(6 \times 2 = 12\) minutes. It shows 12:12 PM.
From 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM is 6 hours, and the clock loses \(6 \times 3 = 18\) minutes. It shows 1:42 PM.
From 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM is 6 hours, three 2-hour spells, and the clock loses \(3 \times 5 = 15\) minutes. It shows 3:45 PM.
From 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM is 12 hours, four 3-hour spells, and the clock gains \(4 \times 8 = 32\) minutes. It shows 9:32 PM.
The clock is 10 minutes fast and loses 2 minutes an hour, so it is right after \(\frac{10}{2} = 5\) hours. That is at 11:00 AM.
The clock is 15 minutes slow and gains 5 minutes an hour, so it is right after \(\frac{15}{5} = 3\) hours. That is at 11:00 AM.
Losing 1 minute in every 10, the clock shows \(\frac{9}{10}\) of the real time passed. In 4 hours (240 minutes) it advances 216 minutes, so it shows 7:36 AM.
The clock is 25 minutes slow and gains 5 minutes an hour, so it is right after \(\frac{25}{5} = 5\) hours. That is at 5:00 PM.

The watch runs 66 minutes for every 60 real ones. It has shown 240 minutes since 10:00 AM, so the real time passed is \(240 \times \frac{60}{66} = 218\frac{2}{11}\) minutes. The actual time is about 1:38 PM.
From 7:00 AM to 5:00 PM is 10 hours, and the clock loses \(10 \times 3 = 30\) minutes. It shows 4:30 PM.
The watch is 18 minutes fast and loses 4 minutes an hour, so it is right after \(\frac{18}{4} = 4.5\) hours. That is at 7:30 PM.
From 11:00 AM to 11:00 PM is 12 hours, four 3-hour spells, and the clock gains \(4 \times 10 = 40\) minutes. It shows 11:40 PM.

The watch runs 56 minutes for every 60 real ones. It has shown 360 minutes since 9:00 AM, so the real time passed is \(360 \times \frac{60}{56} = 385\frac{5}{7}\) minutes. The actual time is about 3:26 PM.
Losing 30 seconds every minute, the clock runs at half speed. It has shown 120 minutes since 5:00 AM, so 240 real minutes have passed and the actual time is 9:00 AM.
From 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM is 8 hours, and the clock gains \(8 \times 9 = 72\) minutes, that is 1 hour 12 minutes. It shows 5:12 PM.
The clock is 40 minutes fast and loses 6 minutes an hour, so it is right after \(\frac{40}{6} = 6\frac{2}{3}\) hours, that is 6 hours 40 minutes. That is at 2:40 PM.
At 3:00 the hands are three hour-marks apart, and each mark is \(30^\circ\). The angle is \(90^\circ\).
At 6:00 the hands are six hour-marks apart, and each mark is \(30^\circ\). The angle is \(180^\circ\).
At 2:00 the hands are two hour-marks apart, and each mark is \(30^\circ\). The angle is \(60^\circ\).
At 9:00 the hands are three hour-marks apart the short way (9 back to 12), and each mark is \(30^\circ\). The angle is \(90^\circ\).
At 4:30 the hour hand is at \(4 \times 30^\circ + 30 \times 0.5^\circ = 135^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(180^\circ\). The angle is \(45^\circ\).
At 12:45 the hour hand is at \(45 \times 0.5^\circ = 22.5^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(270^\circ\), a gap of \(247.5^\circ\). The smaller angle is \(360^\circ - 247.5^\circ = 112.5^\circ\).
At 10:30 the hour hand is at \(10 \times 30^\circ + 30 \times 0.5^\circ = 315^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(180^\circ\). The angle is \(135^\circ\).
At 3:40 the hour hand is at \(3 \times 30^\circ + 40 \times 0.5^\circ = 110^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(240^\circ\). The angle is \(130^\circ\).
At 5:25 the hour hand is at \(5 \times 30^\circ + 25 \times 0.5^\circ = 162.5^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(150^\circ\). The angle is \(12.5^\circ\).
At 11:40 the hour hand is at \(11 \times 30^\circ + 40 \times 0.5^\circ = 350^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(240^\circ\). The angle is \(110^\circ\).
At 6:50 the hour hand is at \(6 \times 30^\circ + 50 \times 0.5^\circ = 205^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(300^\circ\). The angle is \(95^\circ\).
At 8:15 the hour hand is at \(8 \times 30^\circ + 15 \times 0.5^\circ = 247.5^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(90^\circ\). The angle is \(157.5^\circ\).
At 2:25 the hour hand is at \(2 \times 30^\circ + 25 \times 0.5^\circ = 72.5^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(150^\circ\). The angle is \(77.5^\circ\).
At 5:50 the hour hand is at \(5 \times 30^\circ + 50 \times 0.5^\circ = 175^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(300^\circ\). The angle is \(125^\circ\).
At 12:40 the hour hand is at \(40 \times 0.5^\circ = 20^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(240^\circ\), a gap of \(220^\circ\). The smaller angle is \(360^\circ - 220^\circ = 140^\circ\).
At 8:45 the hour hand is at \(8 \times 30^\circ + 45 \times 0.5^\circ = 262.5^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(270^\circ\). The angle is \(7.5^\circ\).
At 9:55 the hour hand is at \(9 \times 30^\circ + 55 \times 0.5^\circ = 297.5^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(330^\circ\). The angle is \(32.5^\circ\).
At 7:40 the hour hand is at \(7 \times 30^\circ + 40 \times 0.5^\circ = 230^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(240^\circ\). The angle is \(10^\circ\).

At 10:10 the hour hand is at \(10 \times 30^\circ + 10 \times 0.5^\circ = 305^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(60^\circ\), a gap of \(245^\circ\). The smaller angle is \(360^\circ - 245^\circ = 115^\circ\).
Buses leave every 30 min and the next is at 10:30, so the last one left at 10:00. It left 10 min before the clerk spoke, so he spoke at 10:10 am.
From 8 to 3 is 7 hours, and the hour hand turns \(30^\circ\) an hour: \(7 \times 30^\circ = 210^\circ\).
At 3:30 the hour hand is at \(90^\circ + 15^\circ = 105^\circ\) and the minute hand at \(180^\circ\), so the angle is \(75^\circ\).
At \(m\) min past 8 the angle is \(240 - 5.5m\) degrees. Opposite hands need \(240 - 5.5m = 180\), so \(m = \frac{60}{5.5} = 10\frac{10}{11}\) min past 8.
4 minute-spaces are \(24^\circ\). At \(m\) min past 3 the angle is \(|90 - 5.5m|\); setting it to 24 gives \(m = 12\) or \(m = \frac{114}{5.5} = 20\frac{8}{11}\).
